name: tsw-safety-netherlands-thejag
title: Safety systems · Netherlands
eyebrow: Signals and train protection · Train Sim World · TCA Quadrant Airbus
sources: Dovetail Games: Zwolle – Groningen ATB guide

paragraphs: Dutch signals show the **speed**, not the route: green, yellow or red, with a lit **number × 10 km/h** below. **Flashing** = the speed applies **from this signal**; steady yellow = **reach it by the next signal**. In TSW 7: **NS ICMm** and **NS SNG** on **Zwolle – Groningen**, under **ATB-EG**, **ATB-Vv** and the **deadman**. Quadrant controls are from TheJAG's profiles.

items.name: ATB-EG
items.summary: Coded track circuits set a ceiling of 40, 60, 80, 130 or 140 km/h. Overspeed rings a bell; brake within ~**3 s** or ATB brakes.
items.where: Whole Zwolle – Groningen line; ICMm and SNG
items.quadrant: Left aux square: ATB fuse (ICMm) / ATB-ERTMS cut-out (SNG)

items.name: ATB-Vv
items.summary: Beacons 120, 30 and 3 m before selected red signals impose a braking curve to a stop. Acts only under code [–] or [BD].
items.where: Selected stop signals on Zwolle – Groningen
items.quadrant: Shares the ATB fuse / cut-out (left aux square)

items.name: Deadman
items.summary: Driver-alive check. Answer the warning in time or the train makes an emergency brake application.
items.quadrant: Gear lever up = acknowledge (game key Q); right aux square = deadman fuse / cut-out

items.name: ATB-NG · ETCS
items.full: ATB nieuwe generatie · European Train Control System
items.summary: ATB-NG (balises, 10 km/h steps) on Dutch diesel lines; ETCS on Betuweroute, HSL-Zuid, Hanzelijn. Not in TSW 7.
items.where: Not on any TSW Dutch route

sections.title: Main signal aspects (hoofdseinen)
sections.note: Lamps top to bottom: green, yellow, red; white number below. Dwarf signals: same colours, max 40 km/h.

items.name: Green (groen)
items.meaning: Proceed at the local (line) speed. ATB code 130 or 140.
items.drive: Accelerate to the speed on the boards.

items.name: Flashing green
items.meaning: Proceed at max 40 km/h from this signal. ATB code [–] 40.
items.drive: Be at 40 km/h passing the signal; usually a diverging route.

items.name: Flashing green + 8
items.meaning: Proceed at max 80 km/h from this signal (number × 10).
items.drive: Hold 80 km/h until a speed board lets you go faster.

items.name: Yellow (geel)
items.meaning: Next signal may be red. Limit speed to 40 km/h. ATB code [–] 40.
items.drive: Brake now to 40 km/h and be ready to stop at the next signal.

items.name: Yellow + 8
items.meaning: Next signal limits to 80 km/h. Reach 80 before it. ATB code [8].
items.drive: Brake to 80 km/h before the next signal.

items.name: Yellow + flashing 6
items.meaning: Limit to 60 km/h; short section, may not be reachable by the next signal.
items.drive: Brake to 60; keep braking if the next signal asks for less.

items.name: Flashing yellow
items.meaning: Drive on sight (rijden op zicht): track beyond may be occupied. Max 40 km/h.
items.drive: Creep, max 40 km/h, able to stop short of any obstruction.

items.name: Red (rood)
items.meaning: Stop before the signal. ATB-EG does not stop you; ATB-Vv may.
items.drive: Stop short of the signal; wait for a proceed aspect.

sections.title: Passing red:
sections.text: ATB-EG never enforces below 40 km/h, so it lets you pass a red signal at up to 40 km/h. Stop short yourself; in TSW only ATB-Vv beacons can save you, and only at selected signals.

sections.title: Boards and other signals
sections.note: Board numbers are × 10 km/h; a small 5 top right adds 5 (12⁵ = 125 km/h).

items.name: P-sein
items.meaning: Automatic block signal (P-bord). Red still means stop.
items.drive: Call the signaller; pass on sight only if no contact is possible.

items.name: Speed reduction
items.drive: Be at 80 km/h by the next white speed board.

items.name: Speed board
items.meaning: Snelheidsbord: local speed beyond the board.
items.drive: Lower: from the front. Higher: once the rear has passed.

items.name: Line speed
items.meaning: Older board: line speed ahead; being replaced by white boards.
items.drive: Accelerate once the rear of the train has passed.

items.name: Train length
items.meaning: Treinlengtebord: stop marker for trains of up to this many cars.
items.drive: ICMm: own car count or next up. 6-car SNG: use 5.

items.name: Departure light
items.meaning: Vertrekseinlicht: the departure procedure may start.
items.drive: Wait for it (and a green) before the doors close.

sections.title: How to drive under ATB-EG and the deadman

blocks.title: Code drops (speed reduction)
steps: A single chime and the cab display shows the lower code, after a short random delay in TSW.
Already below the new ceiling: nothing to do.
Above it (+5 km/h): a continuous bell. Brake within about 3 s.
Make at least a minimum brake application (ICMm step 1 or more, SNG min brake or more); the bell stops.
Three short bells below ceiling +5: you may release the brake.
blocks.note: Brake on time for the signals anyway: ATB only checks you brake, not that you stop in time.

blocks.title: ATB brake (forced brake)
steps: No brake within ~3 s, or overspeed: ATB brakes to a stop; red ATB lamp lit.
When stopped, set full brake on the right throttle: ICMm step 7, SNG Max brake.
Press Ontgrendelen (unlock) in the cab with the mouse; it is not on the Quadrant.
Wait for the red lamp to go out, then release and drive on.

blocks.title: ATB-Vv at red signals
bullets: Acts only under code [–] or [BD]; the beacons are not shown to you.
After the 30 m beacon the limit is 10 km/h (+5).
Over the braking curve: forced brake to a stop.
A release loop up to 60 m before the signal, or a new code above [–], lifts the curve.

blocks.title: Deadman (dodemansinrichting)
steps: Keep the deadman fuse on: right aux square (ICMm fuse, SNG cut-out in).
When the warning sounds, lift the gear lever (game key Q).
Miss it and the train makes an emergency brake application; stop, then recover as the train asks.
blocks.note: The real system is a held pedal or a periodic button; TSW reacts to Q.

blocks.title: Before departure
steps: Left aux square on: ATB fuse (ICMm) or ATB / ERTMS cut-in (SNG). Off gives [BD] and five bells.
Right aux square on: deadman fuse / cut-in.
Check the cab code matches the signal, then pull away.

blocks.title: Boards to know
bullets: Verkenbord: platform ahead at braking distance; start braking for the stop.
CODE board: changeover between ATB-EG and ATB-NG.
A / E boards: start and end of a temporary speed restriction.
